definitions.meaning: the seat of the US government, a capital city
the boy George of legend who chopped down his father's cherry tree, a youthful tree-feller

explanation.definitionFit: The US capital city shares its name with the president whose boyhood story has him felling a cherry tree.

clue.text: Channel swimmer gets direction to go out

parts.note: W is west, a compass direction
the tide ebbs when it goes out

explanation.surface: A cross-Channel swimmer is told which way to head out.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Matthew Webb was the first person to swim the English Channel, in 1875.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Matthew Webb made the first recorded unaided swim across the English Channel.

definitions.meaning: at Trinity College Dublin a manservant attending students is called by this name
the leader of a bowls rink team is so called

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Dublin college attendant and the captain of a team in bowls or curling.

definitions.meaning: cruel handling of a person or animal
a doctor's job is caring for the sick, read as a phrase about sick people

explanation.definitionFit: Cruelty is harsh handling, while a physician's work is caring for those who are unwell.

definitions.meaning: a cereal crop such as wheat or barley grows in the fields
the pattern of fibres running through timber

explanation.definitionFit: Cereal crops are grown in fields, and timber shows a fibrous pattern along its length.

clue.text: One may take a dim view of these people at first

definitions.text: One may take a dim view of these people at first

parts.words: One may take a dim view of these people at first
parts.note: someone whose sight is dim, seeing blurrily, goes first to the eye-test professionals; 'take a dim view' ordinarily means disapprove

explanation.surface: Someone is initially disapproving of a group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a dim view' looks like disapproval; read literally it is someone seeing poorly, who visits these sight-testing people before anything improves.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye professionals test and correct poor vision, so a person seeing dimly goes to them first.

definitions.meaning: a small missile thrown so that it sticks in a dartboard

explanation.definitionFit: A Devon river shares its name with the small missile that pierces a pub game's board.

definitions.meaning: portions handed out to each party
small rented plots of land where people grow vegetables, common in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: Portions dealt out are apportionments, and British rented garden plots are used for growing vegetables.

parts.note: a piece of introductory music would be a composition, but Wordsworth was a poet whose long autobiographical poem bears a musical name

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a composition by the poet Wordsworth.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth wrote no music; his long autobiographical poem carries the title of an introductory musical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's autobiographical poem is titled after a short introductory musical movement.

clue.text: Fish isn't a sort to be supplied in stones

parts.note: brill is a flatfish related to turbot

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange afresh, so the letters of the words before are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A fish that isn't of a particular kind is to be served set in jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges ISNTA (from 'isn't a') into IANTS, which follows the BRILL; 'to be supplied in' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut diamonds of the brilliant cut are themselves called by this plural noun, meaning gems.

parts.note: the line points at itself: the words the solver is reading are the very hint printed for this light

explanation.surface: An excited cry that the moment has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is it!' sounds like excitement; it is literally true of the line being read, which is itself the hint for this light.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed hint the solver reads for any light in a crossword is this very thing.

clue.text: More reckless types enter gamble — confusion results

indicators.note: the reckless sorts go into the wager, so those pieces sit inside it

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
wilder is more reckless
men are types, fellows

explanation.surface: Wilder sorts start betting, and everyone is baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' places WILDER and MEN inside BET; 'results' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bafflement and perplexity are the state of being utterly confused.

clue.text: General takes city. Hamlet preferred by Brooke

parts.note: Ulysses S. Grant, the Union general
Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, England

explanation.surface: A general captures a city; meanwhile a poet favours a small village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' is not Shakespeare's prince but a small village: the Cambridgeshire village Rupert Brooke celebrated in his poem 'The Old Vicarage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke's poem praises this Cambridgeshire village above all other places in England.

clue.text: Sounds a convenient vessel for trade

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase is spoken, giving a word that is said the same way

parts.note: handy means convenient and a craft is a boat or vessel

explanation.surface: A handy boat is said to be good for commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' signals that HANDY CRAFT, a convenient vessel, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual occupation such as pottery or weaving is a trade or craft.

indicators.note: broken up, the letters of one, in and the shield word are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: 21 stands for the answer at 21 down, a small round Highland shield

explanation.surface: One item among twenty-one is damaged during manufacture.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' is a cross-reference to 21 down. 'broken' rearranges ONE, IN and TARGE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing electricity or offspring is generating it, so the act of creation is this noun.

clue.text: Queen gets the port I leave

indicators.note: the letter I is said to leave the port, so it comes out of that name

parts.note: Alexandria is the great Egyptian port

explanation.surface: A queen takes over a harbour city as the narrator departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes I out of ALEXANDRIA. Queen Alexandra was the wife of Edward VII. The ellipsis joins this clue to 17 across, which also uses I and a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra of Denmark was the consort of King Edward VII and so a British royal consort.

clue.text: Express disapproval before cat is put in river

indicators.note: the cat and the before-word are placed within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
pre- is a prefix meaning before
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tuts disapprovingly before a cat is dropped into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put in' places PRE and CAT inside DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak against something or belittle it is to voice disapproval of it.

clue.text: … and I take the port that is best !

parts.note: Deal is a port town on the coast of Kent

explanation.surface: The narrator chooses the finest harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 15 across. Deal is a Kent coastal town, one of the old Cinque Ports.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect or best possible is the model one would wish for.

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of the word before are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone foresees an armed uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges ARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen in sleep or imagined is a vision or fantasy.

clue.text: This cheque may be a present, but not for present presentation

definitions.text: This cheque may be a present, but not for present presentation

parts.words: This cheque may be a present, but not for present presentation
parts.note: a cheque bearing a future date can be given now as a gift, yet the bank will not honour it if shown to them today

explanation.surface: A cheque given as a gift cannot yet be cashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on 'present' three ways: a gift, the current time, and presenting a cheque at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque dated later than when written cannot be paid until that future date arrives.

clue.text: Talks a lot about obscure line in unwelcome correspondence

indicators.note: the talking word surrounds the other letters, placed about them

parts.note: to chatter is to talk a lot

indicators.note: made obscure, the word line is muddled into a different order

explanation.surface: A gossip goes on about a vague sentence in some annoying mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' rearranges LINE to INLE, and 'about' puts it inside CHATTERS, after CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters demanding to be copied and sent on to others are unwanted mail.

clue.text: For self-defence it could be great

definitions.note: the definition describes the purpose of a small shield rather than naming it

indicators.note: says the letters might be arranged differently to form another word

explanation.surface: A great thing might serve for protecting oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could be' rearranges GREAT. A targe is a light round shield, especially a Scottish one.
explanation.definitionFit: A light round Highland shield is carried for personal protection.

indicators.note: the female animal contains the musical letter within it

parts.note: a doe is a female deer
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A woman keeps a memo from a local official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts G inside DOE. The Doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian and Genoese republics were led by an elected chief official of this title.

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting the word turns it upside down, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: tots are small children

explanation.surface: A bullock knocks over some youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' reverses TOTS to read up the grid. A stot is a dialect word for a young bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English and Scots dialect, a bullock or steer is called by this word.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: There is a gap in the very road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters inside 'roAD ITself'. An adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal passage into a mine is an entrance or opening.

definitions.meaning: in Acts 5, Ananias lied to the apostles, fell dead and was borne away by young men

explanation.definitionFit: A task performed is completed, and the Bible says the dead liar's body was borne away for burial.

definitions.meaning: a boy's name, short for Anthony

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means stylish or upmarket, and the same word is a short form of Anthony.

clue.text: Men dispatched again at the start show ill-feeling

parts.note: re-sent means sent again
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of the word the gives only its first letter

explanation.surface: Men sent off once more on arrival display bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes the first letter of 'the', T, to end the answer; 'at' and 'show' only link the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness at being wronged is a grudge, a kind of ill-will.
